adult.regimen: Asthma / COPD exacerbation: 40–50 mg once daily for 5 days (asthma) or 5–7 days (COPD). Katayama: 1 mg/kg/day for 5–7 days.

paediatric.frequency: once daily for 3–5 days (asthma) — no need to taper if course ≤ 7 days.

pregnancy.notes: Acceptable when benefit outweighs risk; betamethasone preferred for foetal lung maturation in preterm labour.

warnings: Live vaccines contraindicated during high-dose therapy and for 3 months after.
Counsel infection risk + steroid-emergency card if on > 5 mg/day for > 3 weeks.
monitoring: Glucose if diabetic; BP; bone health on prolonged courses.

mechanism: GABA-A receptor positive allosteric modulator → CNS depression.

adult.regimen: Status epilepticus: 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) over 2 min, may repeat once after 10 min.

paediatric.frequency: Status epilepticus: 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg).

dosing.hepatic: Preferred benzodiazepine in hepatic impairment (no active metabolites).

pregnancy.notes: Avoid first trimester (small malformation signal); use if benefit clear (status, severe withdrawal).

lactation: Short course acceptable; observe infant sedation.
warnings: Flumazenil 200 µg IV available; avoid flumazenil in chronic-benzodiazepine users (precipitates withdrawal seizures).
monitoring: RR, sedation score, BP every 5 min for first 30 min.

mechanism: GABA-A positive allosteric modulator — same class as lorazepam but longer-acting active metabolites.

adult.regimen: Status: 10 mg IV (5 mg/min) — may repeat once after 10 min.
10–20 mg PR adult / 5 mg < 12 y if no IV access.

paediatric.frequency: Acute convulsion 0.5 mg/kg PR (max 10 mg); may repeat once at 10 min.

pregnancy.notes: Avoid routine use; acceptable in status / severe alcohol withdrawal where benefit clear.

warnings: Active metabolite accumulation in renal / hepatic impairment — prefer lorazepam.
monitoring: RR, sedation score every 5 min.

mechanism: Blocks voltage-gated sodium channels → reduces neuronal firing.

adult.regimen: Status: 20 mg/kg in 0.9 % NaCl at ≤ 50 mg/min with continuous cardiac monitoring (hypotension + bradycardia risk). Maintenance 100 mg every 8 h orally.

paediatric.frequency: Status loading 20 mg/kg at ≤ 1 mg/kg/min with monitoring.

pregnancy.notes: Teratogenic (foetal hydantoin syndrome) but benefit outweighs risk in status / refractory epilepsy. Add folic acid 5 mg daily preconception.

contraindications: Second / third-degree AV block, sinus bradycardia, Stokes–Adams syndrome.
warnings: Narrow therapeutic index — target serum 10–20 mg/L.
Drug interactions: potent CYP enzyme inducer (warfarin, OCPs, DOACs, dolutegravir, atorvastatin).
Extravasation causes 'purple-glove syndrome' — use a large vein and avoid IV push > 50 mg/min.

adverseEffects.effect: Stevens–Johnson syndrome (HLA-B*1502 in Asian populations), hepatitis

monitoring: ECG + BP during IV load. Serum level 1–2 h after load and then at 1 week steady state.

indications.text: Schistosomiasis (S. mansoni, S. haematobium, S. japonicum, S. mekongi)

mechanism: Increases parasite cell-membrane permeability to Ca²⁺ → spastic paralysis of worms; surface tegument disruption.

adult.regimen: Schistosomiasis (mansoni / haematobium): 40 mg/kg single dose with food (or 20 mg/kg × 2 doses 4–6 h apart). S. japonicum / mekongi: 60 mg/kg total (30 mg/kg × 2).

paediatric.frequency: Single dose 40 mg/kg (60 mg/kg for S. japonicum).

pregnancy.notes: Safe and recommended in pregnancy ≥ 14 weeks (WHO 2006 / 2022) — defer in first trimester unless severe disease.

contraindications: Ocular cysticercosis (risk of irreversible retinal damage).
warnings: Avoid in first trimester unless severe disease.
Neurocysticercosis: pre-treat with corticosteroid 1–2 days to reduce inflammatory cyst death.
Drug interactions — rifampicin halves praziquantel levels; CYP3A4 inhibitors increase exposure.
monitoring: Symptom response; re-check eggs / antigen at 8–12 weeks (repeat dose if persistent).

indications.text: Soil-transmitted helminthiasis (ascaris, hookworm, trichuris) — MDA component

mechanism: Selective binding to parasite β-tubulin → impaired glucose uptake and microtubule function.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 / sulphoxidation to active albendazole-sulphoxide.

adult.regimen: STH single dose: 400 mg (200 mg < 2 y). Neurocysticercosis: 7.5 mg/kg twice daily (max 1.2 g) for 8–30 days with food + steroid cover.

paediatric.frequency: STH single dose: 400 mg ≥ 2 y; 200 mg if 1–2 y.

pregnancy.notes: Avoid first trimester (teratogenic in animals). Second / third trimester acceptable in heavy hookworm-related anaemia per WHO.

warnings: Hepatic dysfunction + bone-marrow suppression in long courses (e.g. cysticercosis) — LFT + FBC monitoring.
monitoring: LFT + FBC fortnightly for prolonged courses.

references.label: WHO Guideline on Preventive Chemotherapy for STH (2017)

indications.text: Pulmonary tuberculosis (HRZE first-line, then HR continuation)

mechanism: Binds bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase β-subunit → inhibits transcription. Bactericidal.

adult.regimen: TB: 10 mg/kg once daily (max 600 mg). Take 30 min before food on an empty stomach. Weight-banded 4FDC HRZE (R150/H75/Z400/E275) per WHO band.

paediatric.frequency: 15 mg/kg once daily (range 10–20 mg/kg) on an empty stomach.

pregnancy.notes: Safe; standard first-line in pregnancy. Add vitamin K 10 mg orally to mother in the last 4 weeks (newborn haemorrhage risk).

warnings: Potent CYP3A4, CYP2C9 and P-gp inducer — halves warfarin, OCPs, DOACs, statins, dolutegravir, methadone, ciclosporin, AL, glucocorticoids, ondansetron, tacrolimus.
Counsel patient: harmless orange-red discolouration of urine, sweat, tears (may stain soft contact lenses).

adverseEffects.effect: Drug-induced hepatitis, flu-like syndrome with intermittent dosing

monitoring: Baseline + 2/4/8-weekly ALT, AST, bilirubin during induction phase.

mechanism: Prodrug activated by mycobacterial katG → inhibits inhA, blocks mycolic acid synthesis.

adult.regimen: TB treatment 5 mg/kg once daily (max 300 mg). TPT 6H: 5 mg/kg daily for 6 months. ADD pyridoxine 25–50 mg daily.

paediatric.frequency: 10 mg/kg once daily (range 7–15).

pregnancy.notes: Safe; first-line. Add pyridoxine 50 mg daily.

warnings: Hepatitis risk — counsel patient to report jaundice, anorexia, nausea.
Peripheral neuropathy — co-prescribe pyridoxine in HIV / diabetes / alcohol / pregnancy / breastfeeding / malnutrition.
monitoring: ALT baseline + monthly for first 3 months.

mechanism: Converted to pyrazinoic acid by mycobacterial pyrazinamidase → disrupts membrane energetics and CoA biosynthesis. Active only in acidic phagolysosomes.

adult.regimen: 25 mg/kg once daily (max 2 g) for 2 months as part of HRZE.

paediatric.frequency: 35 mg/kg once daily (30–40 range) for 2 months.

renal.adjustment: Reduce frequency to three times weekly at standard dose; specialist input.

pregnancy.notes: WHO recommends as part of standard regimen in pregnancy (historical reluctance no longer evidence-based).

warnings: Hepatotoxic in combination with R + H — check LFTs.
Hyperuricaemia common.
monitoring: ALT baseline + 2-weekly first month; uric acid if symptomatic gout.

indications.text: Pulmonary tuberculosis (HRZE intensive phase, especially when isoniazid resistance suspected)

mechanism: Inhibits arabinosyl transferase → disrupts mycobacterial cell-wall arabinogalactan.

adult.regimen: 15 mg/kg once daily (max 1.6 g) for 2 months as part of HRZE.

paediatric.frequency: 20 mg/kg once daily (range 15–25).

renal.adjustment: Reduce to 15 mg/kg three times weekly with TDM if available.

pregnancy.notes: Safe.

contraindications: Inability to report visual symptoms (very young children).
warnings: Dose-related optic neuritis — counsel patient to STOP and report any change in visual acuity or colour vision.
Check visual acuity and colour vision at baseline and monthly.

adverseEffects.effect: Optic neuritis (visual blurring, red-green colour blindness)

monitoring: Snellen acuity + Ishihara plates monthly while on therapy.

indications.text: Isoniazid overdose (1 g pyridoxine per 1 g INH ingested)

mechanism: Active form pyridoxal-5-phosphate — co-factor for transaminases, decarboxylases, GABA synthesis.

adult.regimen: INH prophylaxis: 25–50 mg daily (50 mg if HIV / diabetes / alcohol / pregnancy / breastfeeding / malnutrition). INH overdose: 1 g IV per 1 g INH ingested (max 5 g).

paediatric.frequency: 1–2 mg/kg/day during INH-containing TB therapy.

pregnancy.notes: Safe; routinely co-prescribed with isoniazid.

warnings: Chronic high-dose use (≥ 200 mg daily) can paradoxically cause sensory neuropathy.

mechanism: Cytoplasmic phosphorylation to tenofovir diphosphate → competitively inhibits HIV-RT and HBV polymerase + chain termination.

adult.regimen: 300 mg once daily with food (TLD or PrEP). HBV chronic: 300 mg once daily.

paediatric.frequency: Age ≥ 2 / weight ≥ 17 kg per WHO weight-band table (e.g. 17–24 kg = 150 mg).

pregnancy.notes: Safe and recommended in pregnancy (PMTCT first-line in TLD).

warnings: Renal tubular toxicity (proximal tubulopathy / Fanconi syndrome) — check eGFR at baseline, 3 months, then 6-monthly.
Bone loss — supplement vitamin D + calcium in adolescents.
monitoring: eGFR, urine ACR, phosphate at baseline + 3 m + 6-monthly. HBV DNA + ALT 6-monthly.

mechanism: Binds the HIV-1 integrase active site → inhibits proviral DNA strand-transfer into host chromosome.

adult.regimen: 50 mg once daily (TLD). With rifampicin: 50 mg twice daily during rifampicin + 2 weeks after.

paediatric.frequency: WHO paediatric weight bands: 6–10 kg = 5 mg DT × 2, 10–14 kg = 5 mg DT × 3, ≥ 20 kg adult dose 50 mg.

pregnancy.notes: Recommended throughout pregnancy and conception (Tsepamo study no excess neural-tube risk on updated analysis).

warnings: Rifampicin halves DTG exposure — increase to 50 mg twice daily.
Take 2 h before / 6 h after polyvalent cations (Ca, Mg, Fe, Al-antacids).
Modest creatinine rise (inhibits OCT2) is non-pathological.
monitoring: Viral load at month 3, month 6, then 6-monthly. ALT if symptoms.

mechanism: Intracellular phosphorylation → lamivudine-triphosphate → chain-terminator of HIV-RT and HBV-polymerase.

adult.regimen: 300 mg once daily (TLD) or 150 mg twice daily. HBV mono: 100 mg once daily.

paediatric.frequency: 4 mg/kg twice daily (max 150 mg).

pregnancy.notes: Safe; PMTCT first-line component.

warnings: HBV flare on abrupt discontinuation in HBV co-infected patients.
monitoring: Viral load (HIV / HBV) per regimen schedule.

indications.text: Maternal HIV (where DTG not available; legacy regimens)

mechanism: Non-competitive allosteric inhibitor of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase.

adult.regimen: Adult maintenance 200 mg twice daily after 14-day lead-in at 200 mg once daily.

paediatric.frequency: Infant PMTCT: birth–6 weeks 15 mg (1.5 mL of 10 mg/mL); 6 weeks – 6 months 20 mg (2 mL) once daily.

pregnancy.notes: Maternal nevirapine reserved for legacy regimens; infant prophylaxis is the main current use.

warnings: Severe hypersensitivity (rash, hepatitis, Stevens–Johnson syndrome) — risk highest in first 6 weeks; ALT > 5× ULN → stop.
14-day lead-in at half-dose is mandatory.

adverseEffects.effect: Hepatitis, Stevens–Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis

monitoring: ALT baseline + week 2 + week 4 + then 3-monthly during the first year.

indications.text: Bacterial meningitis (Listeria cover, neonates / elderly / immunocompromised)

mechanism: Inhibits cell-wall synthesis via PBP binding.

adult.regimen: Meningitis: 2 g IV every 4 h. Listeria: 2 g IV every 4 h × 3 weeks. Empirical: 1 g every 6 h.

paediatric.frequency: Neonatal sepsis: 50 mg/kg IV every 12 h (week 1) or every 8 h (week 2+). Meningitis: 75 mg/kg every 6 h.

pregnancy.notes: Safe (first-line for asymptomatic bacteriuria / chorio prophylaxis).

warnings: Rash in EBV / leukaemia / allopurinol use.

mechanism: Binds 30S ribosomal subunit → irreversible inhibition of bacterial protein synthesis. Concentration-dependent killing.

adult.regimen: Single daily 5–7 mg/kg ideal-body-weight infusion over 30 min, target peak 15–20 mg/L, trough < 1 mg/L.

paediatric.frequency: Neonatal: 5 mg/kg every 24 h IM/IV (4 mg/kg if < 32 weeks). Children: 7 mg/kg once daily.

renal.adjustment: Same dose, extend interval to every 36 h with trough monitoring.
Avoid where possible; reduce + extend interval with TDM.

pregnancy.notes: Use only when benefit clearly outweighs risk (foetal 8th-cranial-nerve toxicity reported). Acceptable in neonatal/maternal sepsis.

warnings: Nephrotoxic + ototoxic — measure trough before each dose and monitor renal function.
Avoid concurrent furosemide / IV contrast / vancomycin where possible.
monitoring: Trough before each dose; eGFR daily; audiology if course > 7 days.

references.label: WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn, 2013)

indications.text: Measles — all confirmed and suspected cases (age-banded)

mechanism: Retinoic acid → nuclear receptors (RAR/RXR) → epithelial differentiation, immune function, visual pigment regeneration.

adult.regimen: Measles: 200 000 IU today + 200 000 IU tomorrow. Xerophthalmia: 200 000 IU today + tomorrow + after 2 weeks.

paediatric.frequency: Measles age-banded: < 6 m 50 000 IU; 6–11 m 100 000 IU; ≥ 12 m 200 000 IU — today AND tomorrow. Repeat at week 2 if eye signs.

pregnancy.notes: AVOID high-dose vitamin A in pregnancy (> 10 000 IU/day — teratogenic). Low-dose supplementation 10 000 IU is acceptable in severe deficiency only.

lactation: Compatible (single high-dose post-partum permitted per WHO).
warnings: Transient pseudotumour cerebri / vomiting / bulging fontanelle in infants after single high dose — resolves spontaneously.

references.label: WHO Vitamin A Supplementation for Children (2011)

indications.text: Syphilis — primary, secondary, early latent (single dose)
Rheumatic heart disease secondary prophylaxis (monthly × ≥ 10 years)

mechanism: Penicillin G released slowly from depot IM injection — inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis via PBP binding.

adult.regimen: Early syphilis: 2.4 MU IM single dose (1.2 MU each buttock). Late: 2.4 MU IM weekly × 3. RHD prophylaxis: 1.2 MU IM every 21–28 days.

paediatric.frequency: Syphilis ≤ 30 kg: 50 000 IU/kg IM single dose (max 2.4 MU). RHD prophylaxis 1.2 MU IM (< 30 kg: 600 000 IU).

pregnancy.notes: Drug of choice for syphilis in pregnancy. Penicillin allergy → desensitise (NO equivalent alternative for foetal protection).

contraindications: IgE-mediated penicillin hypersensitivity (desensitise in pregnancy / neurosyphilis where no alternative).
warnings: DO NOT give IV (cardiopulmonary toxicity).
Counsel Jarisch–Herxheimer reaction within 6–8 hours of first dose (fever / myalgia) — antipyretics + reassurance.
Pain on injection — consider 1 % lidocaine as diluent.
monitoring: RPR / VDRL titre at 3, 6 and 12 months after treatment — expect 4-fold drop by 6 months.

indications.text: Severe / complicated malaria — first-line parenteral therapy

mechanism: Endoperoxide bridge cleaved by parasite haem → free radicals → parasite kill at all blood stages.

adult.regimen: 2.4 mg/kg IV (or IM) at 0, 12 and 24 h, then once daily until oral therapy tolerated (minimum 24 h parenteral). Follow with full 3-day course of AL.

paediatric.frequency: Children < 20 kg: 3 mg/kg per dose (higher than adult — different PK).

pregnancy.notes: Used in severe malaria in pregnancy throughout all trimesters per WHO (benefit > risk).

warnings: Post-artemisinin delayed haemolysis (PADH) — recheck Hb at day 7 and 28.
monitoring: Parasitaemia daily, blood glucose, electrolytes, Hb at days 7 + 28.

references.label: WHO Guidelines for the Treatment of Malaria 2023

mechanism: Selective α1 + non-selective β blockade (β > α 7:1 IV).

adult.regimen: Severe range BP: 20 mg IV bolus, double dose every 10 min (40, 80, 80 mg) up to 300 mg cumulative; OR infusion 0.5–2 mg/min.
100–200 mg twice daily, titrated to 800 mg/day in 2–3 divided doses.

pregnancy.notes: First-line for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (with methyldopa, nifedipine, hydralazine).

warnings: Avoid in IV cocaine intoxication (unopposed α — paradoxical hypertension).
monitoring: BP, HR every 5 min during IV titration.

indications.text: Severe pre-eclampsia / eclampsia acute BP control
Heart failure (with nitrate, in patients of African descent)

mechanism: Direct arteriolar smooth-muscle relaxation; mechanism incompletely understood (cGMP-related).

adult.regimen: Severe-range BP: 5 mg IV slowly, repeat every 20 min up to 20 mg cumulative.
Chronic 25–50 mg three times daily (max 200 mg/day with concurrent beta-blocker).

pregnancy.notes: Established option for severe hypertension in pregnancy.

warnings: Lupus-like syndrome at doses > 200 mg/day (slow acetylators).
monitoring: BP, HR; ANA if symptoms develop on chronic high doses.

indications.text: Pre-eclampsia / severe hypertension in pregnancy (immediate-release 10 mg orally)

mechanism: Blocks L-type Ca²⁺ channels in vascular smooth muscle → vasodilation.

adult.regimen: Severe-range BP in pregnancy: 10 mg immediate-release orally, repeat every 30 min × max 3 doses, then switch to modified-release. Chronic HTN: 30–60 mg modified-release once daily.

pregnancy.notes: Common option for acute and maintenance pregnancy hypertension.

warnings: AVOID sublingual administration (unpredictable BP drop, stroke risk).
monitoring: BP, HR.

mechanism: Selective β1-blockade → reduces heart rate, contractility, and AV-node conduction.

adult.regimen: 25–50 mg once daily, titrated to 100 mg/day (max 200 mg). Angina 50–100 mg once daily.

renal.adjustment: Reduce to 50 mg every other day.
25 mg every other day or replace with metoprolol.

pregnancy.notes: Avoid first-line in pregnancy (intrauterine growth restriction); labetalol / methyldopa / nifedipine preferred.

lactation: Low transfer but observe infant for bradycardia / hypoglycaemia.
warnings: Mask hypoglycaemia in insulin-treated diabetes — counsel non-adrenergic warning signs.
Do not stop abruptly — taper over 1–2 weeks.
monitoring: HR + BP at each review.

indications.text: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (one of the four GDMT pillars)

mechanism: Highly selective β1-blockade.

adult.regimen: HFrEF: start 1.25 mg once daily, double every 2 weeks as tolerated up to target 10 mg once daily. Hypertension: 5–10 mg once daily.

pregnancy.notes: Use only if benefit > risk; labetalol preferred for HTN in pregnancy.

warnings: Initiate ONLY when haemodynamically stable in HFrEF. Up-titrate slowly — target heart rate 60–70 / SBP > 90.
monitoring: HR, BP, weight, symptoms at every titration step.

mechanism: Active metabolite α-methyl-noradrenaline → central α2-agonism → reduced sympathetic outflow.

adult.regimen: 250 mg twice or three times daily; titrate every 2 days to max 3 g/day in divided doses.

pregnancy.notes: First-line antihypertensive for chronic hypertension in pregnancy — longest safety record.

warnings: Coombs-positive haemolytic anaemia, hepatitis with chronic use; check LFTs + Coombs annually if long-term.
monitoring: BP at each ANC visit; LFTs + direct Coombs at 6 weeks then 6-monthly on chronic therapy.

mechanism: Provides elemental iron for haemoglobin synthesis (200 mg ferrous sulphate ≈ 65 mg elemental iron).

adult.regimen: Anaemia treatment: 200 mg once daily on an empty stomach with vitamin C, OR alternate-day dosing (WHO 2022 — improves absorption). Pregnancy IFA: 60 mg elemental iron + 400 µg folic acid once daily.

paediatric.frequency: 3 mg/kg/day elemental iron in 1–2 divided doses.

pregnancy.notes: Recommended antenatal supplementation in all settings; treatment doses in confirmed IDA.

contraindications: Iron-storage disease (haemochromatosis, thalassaemia trait under specialist).
warnings: Counsel dark stools, GI upset, constipation — common but transient.
Separate from tetracyclines / fluoroquinolones / dolutegravir / levothyroxine by 2 hours (chelation).
monitoring: Hb at 4–6 weeks; expect 1–2 g/dL rise. Continue 3 months after Hb target to replenish stores.

mechanism: Converted to tetrahydrofolate — cofactor for purine + thymidylate synthesis (DNA).

adult.regimen: Routine pregnancy / pre-conception: 400 µg daily from 1 month pre-conception until end of week 12. High-risk (previous NTD, diabetes, antiepileptics): 5 mg daily. SCD: 5 mg daily lifelong. Folate-deficiency anaemia: 5 mg daily for 4 months.

paediatric.frequency: SCD child: 1–5 mg daily (1 mg < 5 y; 5 mg ≥ 5 y).

pregnancy.notes: Recommended for all pregnancies; 5 mg in high-risk.

contraindications: Pernicious anaemia (B12 deficiency) without concurrent B12 — masks neurological deterioration.
warnings: Exclude B12 deficiency before treating macrocytic anaemia with folate alone.
monitoring: FBC at 1–4 months in megaloblastic anaemia.

indications.text: Intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (IPTp-SP) for malaria in high-transmission settings
Seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) in Sahel (with amodiaquine)

mechanism: Sulfadoxine inhibits dihydropteroate synthase; pyrimethamine inhibits dihydrofolate reductase — synergistic blockade of plasmodial folate synthesis.

adult.regimen: IPTp-SP: 3 tablets (1500 mg sulfadoxine + 75 mg pyrimethamine) at each ANC contact after week 13, at least 1 month apart, minimum 3 doses by delivery.

paediatric.frequency: SMC: 250 mg sulfadoxine + 12.5 mg pyrimethamine (single dose) per cycle.

pregnancy.notes: IPTp-SP is the standard of care in moderate-to-high malaria-transmission areas from week 13 onwards. Avoid before week 13 (folate-antagonism teratogenicity).

lactation: Avoid; can cause kernicterus in jaundiced infant (sulfonamide).
warnings: Stevens–Johnson syndrome reported; counsel rash + mucositis warning signs.
monitoring: Symptom check; no routine labs.

drugClass: Concentrated dextrose for IV hypoglycaemia rescue
mechanism: Rapid IV substrate replacement — restores plasma glucose.

adult.regimen: Hypoglycaemia: 50 mL of 50 % dextrose IV (25 g) over 1–3 min into a large vein; flush. May repeat 25 mL bolus if persistent.

paediatric.frequency: Use 10 % dextrose 2 mL/kg IV in children (avoid 50 % — sclerosis risk).

pregnancy.notes: Safe in maternal hypoglycaemia.

contraindications: No absolute contraindication in life-threatening hypoglycaemia.
warnings: STRICTLY for large-vein IV use — extravasation causes tissue necrosis.
In sulphonylurea-induced hypoglycaemia, follow with 10 % dextrose infusion + octreotide where available — recurrence is high.
In chronic alcohol use, give thiamine 100 mg IV before / with glucose (Wernicke prevention).

adverseEffects.effect: Local vein irritation, hyperglycaemia in non-diabetics

monitoring: Recheck capillary glucose at 5 and 15 min; 10 % dextrose infusion if recurrence.

mechanism: Provides isotonic sodium-chloride solution (154 mmol/L Na, 154 mmol/L Cl).

adult.regimen: Septic / hypovolaemic shock: 30 mL/kg bolus (typically 1–2 L) in the first hour, reassess and titrate. Maintenance: 25–30 mL/kg/24 h.

paediatric.frequency: Shock: 20 mL/kg bolus over 15–30 min, repeat once. Maintenance: Holliday–Segar formula (100 mL/kg first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg next 10 kg, 20 mL/kg thereafter).

pregnancy.notes: Safe.

contraindications: Hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis (use Ringer's lactate instead).
Severe heart failure unable to handle volume.
warnings: Large volumes cause hyperchloraemic acidosis — prefer balanced crystalloid (Ringer's) where available for > 2 L resuscitation.

adverseEffects.effect: Hyperchloraemic metabolic acidosis at high volumes

monitoring: U&E, urine output, lung exam at 4-hourly intervals during resuscitation.

indications.text: Septic / hypovolaemic shock (balanced crystalloid first-line per Surviving Sepsis 2021)

mechanism: Isotonic solution with Na 131, Cl 111, K 5, Ca 2, lactate 29 mmol/L (lactate metabolised to bicarbonate in liver — pH neutral).

adult.regimen: Resuscitation: 30 mL/kg over the first hour, then titrated. Burns: Parkland 4 mL/kg × % TBSA — half in first 8 h.

paediatric.frequency: Shock 20 mL/kg bolus over 15–30 min.

pregnancy.notes: Safe.

contraindications: Hyperkalaemia (contains K⁺ 5 mmol/L — avoid in K⁺ > 6).
Severe lactic acidosis with hepatic dysfunction (cannot metabolise lactate).
warnings: Avoid co-infusion with ceftriaxone in the same line (calcium-ceftriaxone precipitation).

adverseEffects.effect: Fluid overload, hyperkalaemia in renal failure

monitoring: U&E, lactate, urine output during resuscitation.

mechanism: Inhibits fungal CYP51 (lanosterol 14-α demethylase) → reduced ergosterol → cell-membrane disruption.

adult.regimen: Vaginal candidiasis: 150 mg single oral dose. Oropharyngeal candidiasis: 100 mg daily × 7–14 d. Cryptococcal meningitis consolidation: 800 mg daily × 8 wks; maintenance 200 mg daily until CD4 > 200 for 6 m.
Same dose IV when oral not tolerated.

paediatric.frequency: 6 mg/kg/day for systemic infection.

pregnancy.notes: Single 150 mg dose acceptable for vaginal candidiasis from second trimester. Avoid high-dose chronic therapy in first trimester (teratogenicity reported).

warnings: Potent CYP2C9 + moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor — interacts with warfarin (INR rise), phenytoin, atorvastatin, sulphonylureas.
QT prolongation — caution with other QT drugs / hypokalaemia.
monitoring: LFTs at baseline + every 2 weeks on chronic high-dose; INR for patients on warfarin.

references.label: WHO Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of cryptococcal disease (2022)

indications.text: Herpes simplex (HSV-1 / HSV-2) — orolabial, genital, encephalitis
Varicella-zoster — shingles (zoster), severe chickenpox in immunocompromised

mechanism: Phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase → aciclovir-triphosphate inhibits viral DNA polymerase and terminates chain.

adult.regimen: HSV genital first episode: 400 mg three times daily × 7–10 d. Recurrent: 800 mg twice daily × 5 d. Zoster: 800 mg five times daily × 7 d.
HSV encephalitis: 10 mg/kg every 8 h × 14–21 d, infused over 1 h with hydration.

paediatric.frequency: Neonatal HSV: 20 mg/kg every 8 h × 14 d (mucocutaneous) or 21 d (CNS / disseminated).

pregnancy.notes: Safe across pregnancy; first-line for HSV in pregnancy.

warnings: Ensure adequate hydration (500 mL fluid per IV dose) — crystal nephropathy at high IV doses in dehydration.

adverseEffects.effect: Acute kidney injury, neurotoxicity (high IV doses)

monitoring: Renal function on IV therapy; urinalysis.

indications.text: Opioid overdose / iatrogenic opioid-induced respiratory depression

mechanism: Competitive antagonist at µ-opioid receptors → rapid reversal of opioid effects.

adult.regimen: 400 µg IV bolus, repeat every 2–3 min as needed (max 10 mg before reconsidering diagnosis). Maintenance infusion 60 % of effective dose per hour for long-acting opioids (methadone, MR opioids).
400–800 µg IM if no IV access (out-of-hospital, peer use).

paediatric.frequency: 10 µg/kg per dose IV, repeat every 2–3 min.

pregnancy.notes: Safe — risk of foetal harm from maternal respiratory arrest outweighs any theoretical risk.

warnings: Re-sedation risk: half-life shorter than most opioids — observe minimum 4 hours after last naloxone dose, longer for methadone / MR opioids.
Precipitates acute withdrawal in chronic opioid users — start with lower dose (40–100 µg) where withdrawal is a concern.
monitoring: RR, sedation, SpO₂ continuously; consider HDU for long-acting opioids.

references.label: WHO Community management of opioid overdose (2014)

mechanism: Restores extracellular calcium → stabilises myocardial membrane potential, reverses neuromuscular hyperexcitability of hypocalcaemia.

adult.regimen: Hyperkalaemia + ECG changes: 10 mL of 10 % calcium gluconate IV over 10 min — onset 1–3 min, repeat every 10 min if ECG changes persist. Magnesium toxicity: same dose. Severe hypocalcaemia: 10–20 mL of 10 % over 10 min.

paediatric.frequency: 0.5 mL/kg of 10 % calcium gluconate over 10 min.

pregnancy.notes: Safe in eclampsia / hypocalcaemia.

warnings: Extravasation causes tissue necrosis — large vein, slow push.
Calcium chloride contains 3× more elemental calcium per mL — central line preferred.

adverseEffects.effect: Flushing, hypotension, bradycardia on rapid injection

monitoring: ECG continuous during administration; serum calcium 1 h post-dose.

indications.text: Severe metabolic acidosis (pH < 7.10) in cardiac arrest, AKI, lactic acidosis

mechanism: Provides bicarbonate → buffers H⁺ → raises serum and urinary pH.

adult.regimen: Severe acidosis (pH < 7.10): 50–100 mEq IV slow bolus, recheck ABG; target pH 7.20 (NOT normal pH). Salicylate poisoning: 1–2 mEq/kg bolus then 100–150 mEq in 1 L D5W at 250 mL/h, target urine pH 7.5–8.

pregnancy.notes: Safe in indicated emergencies.

warnings: AVOID routine use in DKA / lactic acidosis — worsens intracellular acidosis (Bohr effect) and CSF acidosis.
Hypernatraemia, hypokalaemia, calcium binding.

adverseEffects.effect: Hypernatraemia, fluid overload, hypokalaemia, paradoxical CNS acidosis

monitoring: ABG before and 30 min after; Na, K, ionised Ca.

indications.text: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (alternative to ACE-i)

mechanism: Selective AT1 receptor blockade → vasodilation, reduced aldosterone, reduced sympathetic tone.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2C9 to active EXP-3174 (longer t½).

adult.regimen: Hypertension: start 50 mg once daily, titrate to 100 mg daily. HFrEF / proteinuria: up-titrate as tolerated to 150 mg daily. Reduce starting dose to 25 mg in elderly, hepatic impairment, hypovolaemia.

renal.adjustment: Start 25 mg once daily; titrate cautiously with K⁺ + creatinine monitoring.

pregnancy.notes: TERATOGENIC — second / third trimester causes oligohydramnios, renal failure, skull hypoplasia. Stop before conception attempt; use methyldopa / labetalol / nifedipine instead.

lactation: Avoid; switch to ACE-i (captopril / enalapril) where possible (limited milk transfer).
warnings: Hyperkalaemia — additive with spironolactone, cotrimoxazole, K⁺ supplements.
First-dose hypotension in volume-depleted patients.
monitoring: U&E + creatinine at 2 weeks of any dose change; potassium.

indications.text: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (MRA — one of four GDMT pillars)
Ascites of liver cirrhosis (with furosemide 100:40 ratio)

mechanism: Competitive aldosterone-receptor antagonist in distal tubule → natriuresis, K⁺ + H⁺ sparing.

adult.regimen: HFrEF: start 25 mg once daily, titrate to 50 mg if K⁺ remains < 5 and creatinine stable. Cirrhotic ascites: start 100 mg daily, up to 400 mg/day. Resistant HTN: 25 mg once daily.

renal.adjustment: AVOID in eGFR < 30 (hyperkalaemia risk); specialist input.

pregnancy.notes: Avoid — antiandrogenic effects on male foetus; use alternative diuretics if needed.

warnings: Hyperkalaemia + AKI — additive with ACE-i / ARB / cotrimoxazole / K⁺ supplements; check K⁺ + creatinine within 1 week.
Gynaecomastia (10 % at 1 year), menstrual irregularity — switch to eplerenone if intolerable.
monitoring: U&E, K⁺, creatinine within 1 week of start / dose change; 3-monthly thereafter.

indications.text: Adjunct in bacterial meningitis (before / with first antibiotic dose)
Antenatal corticosteroid for foetal lung maturation (24–34 weeks)

mechanism: Potent glucocorticoid — 25× hydrocortisone, no mineralocorticoid activity.

adult.regimen: Bacterial meningitis: 0.15 mg/kg IV every 6 h × 4 days (10 mg in adult, ideally with or 15 min before first antibiotic). Cerebral oedema: 8 mg IV every 6 h. COVID-19: 6 mg IV / orally daily × 10 d.
Croup single dose 0.15–0.6 mg/kg (max 16 mg). Antenatal lung maturation: 6 mg IM every 12 h × 4 doses.

paediatric.frequency: Meningitis 0.15 mg/kg every 6 h × 4 days. Croup single dose 0.15–0.6 mg/kg.

pregnancy.notes: First-line for foetal lung maturation 24–34 weeks gestation when preterm delivery anticipated within 7 days.

warnings: Hyperglycaemia, mood disturbance, insomnia, infection risk. Steroid-emergency card if > 3 weeks of treatment.

adverseEffects.effect: Hyperglycaemia, insomnia, mood change, increased appetite

monitoring: Glucose; BP.

indications.text: Major depressive disorder (first-line per WHO mhGAP)

mechanism: Selective inhibition of serotonin reuptake at presynaptic terminals.

adult.regimen: Start 50 mg once daily in the morning. Titrate by 50 mg every 2–4 weeks; max 200 mg/day. Reduce to 25 mg start in panic disorder / elderly / hepatic impairment.

paediatric.frequency: Off-label use in OCD ≥ 6 y at specialist input only.

pregnancy.notes: Preferred SSRI in pregnancy + breastfeeding; modest neonatal serotonin syndrome risk if used near term (mostly transient).

lactation: Preferred SSRI during breastfeeding (low milk transfer).
warnings: Suicidal ideation worsening in first 4 weeks — close follow-up in patients < 25 y.
Hyponatraemia / SIADH especially in elderly.
QT prolongation at high doses.
Discontinuation syndrome — taper over 4–6 weeks.

adverseEffects.effect: GI upset, headache, sexual dysfunction, insomnia, anxiety in first 2 weeks

monitoring: PHQ-9 at 2, 4 and 8 weeks; sodium at 1 month in elderly.

mechanism: High-affinity D2-receptor antagonism in mesolimbic and nigrostriatal pathways; also α1 and 5-HT2A blockade.

adult.regimen: Acute psychosis 2.5–10 mg orally every 4–8 h titrated; maintenance 5–10 mg daily in divided doses. Delirium / agitation 0.5–2 mg orally (or IM) every 4 h.
Acute agitation 2.5–10 mg IM, repeat after 30–60 min if needed (max 18 mg / 24 h).

paediatric.frequency: Specialist use only; mhGAP allows 1–5 mg/day for severe agitation in older children.

pregnancy.notes: Risk of extrapyramidal symptoms + withdrawal in neonate if used in third trimester. Use only if benefit clear (acute psychosis); olanzapine often preferred.

contraindications: Parkinson's disease and Lewy-body dementia (severe EPS).
warnings: QT prolongation — baseline ECG; avoid in long-QT, hypokalaemia, concurrent QT-prolonging drugs (ondansetron, azithromycin, fluconazole).
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) — fever, rigidity, autonomic instability → stop drug, supportive care, dantrolene / bromocriptine.
Acute dystonia (especially young men) → treat with procyclidine or diphenhydramine.

adverseEffects.effect: Sedation, extrapyramidal symptoms, tardive dyskinesia (chronic), QT prolongation

monitoring: ECG at baseline + after dose change; AIMS / Simpson-Angus scales for EPS / tardive dyskinesia.

mechanism: Multi-receptor antagonism: D2, 5-HT2A, 5-HT2C, H1, α1, M1.

adult.regimen: Schizophrenia: 5–10 mg once daily, titrate to 10–20 mg/day. Acute mania: 10–15 mg once daily.
Acute agitation: 10 mg IM; max 30 mg / 24 h. Avoid IM benzodiazepine within 1 h (hypotension risk).

pregnancy.notes: Limited data; preferred to haloperidol in many series. Counsel risk of neonatal extrapyramidal / withdrawal symptoms in third trimester.

lactation: Avoid where alternative available; monitor infant sedation.
warnings: Metabolic syndrome — weight gain (5–10 kg), dyslipidaemia, T2DM. Baseline + 3-monthly weight / glucose / lipids.
Sedation, postural hypotension (titrate slowly in elderly).
monitoring: Weight, BP, fasting glucose, lipid profile at baseline + 3 m + annually.

references.label: NICE CG178 — Psychosis and schizophrenia in adults (2014)

indications.text: Depression (less commonly first-line; TCA reserved when SSRI fails)

mechanism: Mixed serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibition + anticholinergic + α1 + H1 blockade.

adult.regimen: Neuropathic pain / migraine: 10–25 mg at night, titrate to 75 mg (max 150 mg) over 4–6 weeks. Depression: 75–150 mg daily, specialist if higher.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data; SSRI preferred for new prescriptions. Risk of neonatal anticholinergic / withdrawal effects in third trimester.

warnings: Severe overdose toxicity — narrow therapeutic window. ECG within 6 h if intentional overdose.
Anticholinergic — caution in BPH, glaucoma, elderly (falls, delirium).
Suicide-risk — consider sertraline as safer alternative in high-risk patients.

adverseEffects.effect: Dry mouth, drowsiness, constipation, urinary retention, weight gain, postural hypotension

monitoring: BP, ECG in elderly / cardiac disease.

references.label: NICE CG173 — Neuropathic pain in adults (2013, updated)

indications.text: Gout (chronic urate-lowering therapy after acute flare)

mechanism: Inhibits xanthine oxidase → reduces conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid → falls in serum urate.

adult.regimen: Start 100 mg once daily, titrate by 100 mg every 2–4 weeks to target urate < 360 µmol/L (or < 300 with tophi). Usual maintenance 300–600 mg/day, max 900 mg.

renal.adjustment: Start 50 mg every other day; titrate to target urate.
Start 50 mg every other day; rarely exceed 100 mg/day; consider febuxostat alternative.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data; specialist use only.

contraindications: HLA-B*5801 positive without specialist input (Han Chinese, Thai, Korean — high SCAR risk).
warnings: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (DRESS, Stevens–Johnson, TEN) — risk highest in Asian descent, CKD, concurrent thiazide, recent start. Stop at FIRST sign of rash.
Co-prescribe NSAID / colchicine / low-dose prednisolone for the first 6 months to prevent paradoxical flares.
Severe interaction with azathioprine and 6-mercaptopurine — reduce thiopurine dose by 75 % or avoid.

adverseEffects.effect: Rash (2 %), GI upset, transient flare of gout

monitoring: Serum urate every 2–4 weeks during titration; FBC + LFT 6-monthly. HLA-B*5801 screen before initiation in at-risk ethnicities where feasible.

mechanism: Exogenous T4 → peripheral 5'-deiodinase converts to T3 (active) → nuclear receptor activation → cellular metabolism.

adult.regimen: Healthy adult: 1.6 µg/kg/day (typical start 50–100 µg once daily, on empty stomach 30–60 min before food / coffee). Elderly / cardiac disease: start 25 µg, titrate by 25 µg every 4–6 weeks per TSH.

paediatric.frequency: Newborn: 10–15 µg/kg/day; reduced with age.

pregnancy.notes: Increase pre-pregnancy dose by 25–30 % at confirmation of pregnancy. Target TSH < 2.5 mIU/L in first trimester.

warnings: Cardiac risk in elderly / IHD — start low, titrate slowly.
Many drugs interfere with absorption: iron, calcium, antacids, PPIs, soy, coffee, cholestyramine — separate by 4 h.
Generic brand switches change bioavailability — keep same brand where possible.

adverseEffects.effect: Over-replacement symptoms — tachycardia, tremor, weight loss, insomnia, osteopenia (chronic)

monitoring: TSH at 6–8 weeks after any dose change, then 6-monthly when stable.

indications.text: Hyperemesis gravidarum (second-line after antihistamine + metoclopramide failure)

mechanism: Selective serotonin 5-HT3 antagonism at vagal afferents + chemoreceptor trigger zone.

adult.regimen: 4–8 mg every 8 h orally (max 24 mg/day).
4–8 mg IV / IM slowly every 8 h.

paediatric.frequency: 0.15 mg/kg/dose IV (max 4 mg) every 8 h; PO 4 mg ≥ 6 y.

pregnancy.notes: Limited weak evidence of cleft palate at high doses early; use in hyperemesis gravidarum after failure of pyridoxine + doxylamine + metoclopramide.

warnings: QT prolongation — avoid > 16 mg single IV dose; baseline ECG if multiple QT-prolonging drugs; correct K⁺ / Mg first.
Serotonin syndrome with SSRIs / MAOIs (rare).
monitoring: ECG (QTc) if risk factors.

references.label: WHO Anti-emetics for adults in palliative care

indications.text: Moderate acute pain unresponsive to NSAID / paracetamol

mechanism: µ-opioid agonist (weak) + inhibits noradrenaline + serotonin reuptake.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic CYP2D6 to O-desmethyltramadol (active, more potent µ-agonist). CYP3A4 minor.

adult.regimen: 50–100 mg orally every 4–6 h (max 400 mg/day). Modified-release 100 mg twice daily, max 400 mg/day.
50–100 mg slow IV every 4–6 h.

renal.adjustment: Reduce to every 12 h, max 200 mg/day.

pregnancy.notes: Avoid in pregnancy (neonatal withdrawal, seizures). Use paracetamol / brief codeine alternative.

lactation: Avoid where possible; risk of neonatal sedation in CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolisers.
warnings: Lowers seizure threshold — avoid in epilepsy / head injury / alcohol withdrawal / concurrent SSRI.
Serotonin syndrome with SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, triptans, methylene blue, ondansetron, linezolid.
Dependence + abuse potential — taper after > 2 weeks.

adverseEffects.effect: Dizziness, nausea, constipation, sweating, dry mouth

monitoring: Pain score; sedation if higher dose.

mechanism: Binds glutamate-gated chloride channels in parasite nerve / muscle → hyperpolarisation → paralysis. Selective for invertebrate channels.

adult.regimen: Scabies: 200 µg/kg orally on day 1 and day 8 (and day 15 for crusted scabies). Strongyloidiasis: 200 µg/kg single dose, repeat at 2 weeks in immunocompromised. Onchocerciasis: 150 µg/kg single dose annually (every 6 months in heavy infection).

paediatric.frequency: Children ≥ 15 kg only: 200 µg/kg single dose. Same scheduling as adults.

pregnancy.notes: Generally avoided in pregnancy (limited safety data); WHO does include in MDA accidentally — usually no harm but defer routine use.

lactation: Avoid in first week post-partum; otherwise low transfer acceptable.
warnings: Loa loa co-infection → severe post-treatment encephalopathy in Loa-endemic areas (Central Africa); screen with Loa antigen / nested PCR before MDA.
Counsel itching as treatment response (Mazzotti reaction).

adverseEffects.effect: Pruritus, transient lymphadenopathy (Mazzotti reaction in onchocerciasis)
Postural hypotension, encephalopathy (in Loa loa co-infection)

monitoring: Symptomatic; CD4 + viral load if HIV + crusted scabies.

mechanism: Stabilises sodium channels in parasite nerve membranes → paralysis and death.

adult.regimen: Scabies: apply 5 % cream to entire body neck-to-toe (include face / scalp in infants and elderly); leave 8–14 h overnight; wash off. Repeat after 7 days. Head lice: apply to wet hair / scalp, leave 10 min, rinse; repeat at day 7.

paediatric.frequency: Same regimen as adult; safe from age 2 months.

pregnancy.notes: Safe (minimal absorption). First-line scabies treatment in pregnancy and breastfeeding.

warnings: Treat all close contacts simultaneously. Wash clothing / bedding at ≥ 50 °C or seal for 72 hours.
Itching often persists 2–4 weeks after successful treatment — antihistamines + emollients.

drugClass: Amide local anaesthetic / class Ib antiarrhythmic

indications.text: Local infiltration anaesthesia (wound suturing, IV insertion)
Ventricular tachycardia / fibrillation (refractory — class Ib antiarrhythmic, second-line to amiodarone in arrest)

mechanism: Reversible sodium-channel blockade → blocks nerve conduction (use-dependent).

adult.regimen: Plain 1 % (10 mg/mL): max 3 mg/kg (≈ 200 mg in 70 kg adult). With adrenaline 1:200 000: max 7 mg/kg (≈ 500 mg).
Refractory VF / pulseless VT: 100 mg IV bolus (or 1–1.5 mg/kg), repeat 0.5–0.75 mg/kg every 5–10 min up to 3 mg/kg cumulative.

paediatric.frequency: Max 3 mg/kg plain, 7 mg/kg with adrenaline.

pregnancy.notes: Safe for local anaesthesia and antiarrhythmic use.

contraindications: Avoid adrenaline-containing solutions in end-arterial sites (digits, penis, nose).
warnings: Systemic LA toxicity — perioral tingling, metallic taste, tinnitus, seizures, cardiac arrest. Aspirate before injection; max-dose calculation by weight.
Intralipid 20 % 1.5 mL/kg IV bolus for refractory LA toxicity (LipidRescue).

adverseEffects.effect: Methaemoglobinaemia (high dose topical / EMLA in neonates), local tissue irritation

monitoring: BP, HR + ECG for IV antiarrhythmic use.

indications.text: Oncological — leukaemia, lymphoma (high-dose with folinic-acid rescue)
Ectopic pregnancy (medical management — single 50 mg/m² IM)

mechanism: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase → blocks DNA / RNA / protein synthesis; immunomodulatory at low weekly doses.

adult.regimen: Rheumatoid arthritis: 7.5–10 mg ONCE WEEKLY oral, titrate by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks to 20–25 mg/week as tolerated. Always co-prescribe folic acid 5 mg ONCE WEEKLY (different day from MTX).
Ectopic pregnancy: 50 mg/m² IM single dose with beta-hCG follow-up.

renal.adjustment: AVOID — risk of severe toxicity; switch DMARD.

pregnancy.notes: TERATOGENIC + abortifacient — stop 3 months before conception attempt (men + women). Reliable contraception during therapy.

warnings: NEVER prescribe daily — once-weekly is the standard for RA / psoriasis. Daily dosing causes lethal pancytopenia.
Bone-marrow suppression, hepatotoxicity, pneumonitis, mucositis.
Folate antagonism — fatal interaction with cotrimoxazole (additive bone-marrow suppression).
NSAIDs reduce renal clearance — bone-marrow suppression risk.
Live vaccines contraindicated.

adverseEffects.effect: Nausea, mouth ulcers, alopecia, raised ALT

monitoring: FBC + LFT + U&E baseline, then 2-weekly for first 3 months, then 4–8-weekly. Chest signs / dyspnoea → CXR for pneumonitis.

references.label: EULAR Recommendations for the management of RA (2022)

indications.text: Rheumatic-heart-disease secondary prophylaxis (oral alternative to monthly benzathine)
Sickle-cell disease — paediatric prophylaxis to age 5 (10 y in some programmes)

mechanism: Inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis via PBP binding (penicillin G analogue with oral bioavailability).

adult.regimen: Strep throat: 500 mg twice daily for 10 days. RHD prophylaxis: 250 mg twice daily lifelong (or until age 21 minimum).

paediatric.frequency: SCD prophylaxis: 62.5 mg twice daily (birth–1 y), 125 mg twice daily (1–3 y), 250 mg twice daily (≥ 3 y). RHD prophylaxis: 250 mg twice daily ≥ 5 y.

pregnancy.notes: Safe.

warnings: Counsel adherence — RHD prophylaxis failure due to oral non-adherence is well documented; consider monthly benzathine for high-risk patients.

references.label: WHF Position Paper on Secondary Prophylaxis for RHD

indications.text: Stress-ulcer prophylaxis in ICU (alternative to PPI)

mechanism: Forms viscous gel binding to ulcer crater → physical barrier; stimulates prostaglandin + mucus production.

adult.regimen: 1 g four times daily on empty stomach (1 h before meals + at bedtime) for 4–8 weeks.

pregnancy.notes: Acceptable; minimal systemic absorption.

warnings: Reduces absorption of many drugs (warfarin, fluoroquinolones, digoxin, levothyroxine, phenytoin) — separate by 2 hours.
Aluminium accumulation in dialysis patients — avoid.

indications.text: Sickle-cell disease — reduces vaso-occlusive crises, ACS, transfusion need (≥ 9 months old)

mechanism: Inhibits ribonucleotide reductase → blocks DNA synthesis; in SCD, increases foetal haemoglobin (HbF) production.

adult.regimen: SCD adult: start 15 mg/kg once daily, titrate every 8 weeks by 5 mg/kg targeting maximum tolerated dose (target MCV 100–110 fL and ANC 2–4 × 10⁹/L; max 35 mg/kg/day).

paediatric.frequency: ≥ 9 months: start 20 mg/kg once daily; titrate similarly.

renal.adjustment: Reduce dose by 50 % at start; titrate cautiously.

pregnancy.notes: Avoid in pregnancy (teratogenic in animals). Stop 3 months before conception attempt. Counsel both partners (cytotoxic).

warnings: Bone-marrow suppression — FBC every 2 weeks until stable dose, then 3-monthly.
Co-prescribe folic acid 5 mg daily.
Counsel cytotoxic precautions for caregivers handling tablets / vomit / body fluids.

adverseEffects.effect: Myelosuppression, GI upset, skin pigmentation, nail changes

monitoring: FBC, reticulocytes, HbF % at baseline, every 2 weeks until stable, then 3-monthly. LFT + U&E 6-monthly.

mechanism: Binds 50S ribosomal subunit → inhibits bacterial protein synthesis; bacteriostatic.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic CYP3A4 (potent inhibitor of own enzyme + many substrates).

adult.regimen: Standard: 500 mg twice daily for 5–14 days. H. pylori: 500 mg twice daily × 14 days as part of PPI + amoxicillin triple therapy.

paediatric.frequency: 7.5 mg/kg twice daily (max 500 mg).

pregnancy.notes: Avoid in first trimester (limited human data); use azithromycin / amoxicillin if alternative.

contraindications: Concurrent ergot derivatives, pimozide, lovastatin, simvastatin, colchicine in renal impairment, ticagrelor.
warnings: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitor — increases atorvastatin (rhabdomyolysis), warfarin (INR rise), tacrolimus, ciclosporin, midazolam, sildenafil, dolutegravir (minor).
QT prolongation — cardiac death signal in MS coronary disease.

adverseEffects.effect: Torsades de pointes, severe cutaneous reactions, C. difficile

monitoring: ECG if QT risk factors; LFT if course > 14 days.

references.label: Maastricht VI Consensus on H. pylori

indications.text: Dermatophyte infections — tinea pedis, corporis, cruris, capitis
Onychomycosis (oral therapy 6–12 weeks fingernails / 12–24 weeks toenails)

mechanism: Inhibits fungal squalene epoxidase → ergosterol depletion + squalene accumulation → fungal cell death.

adult.regimen: Onychomycosis: 250 mg once daily for 6–12 weeks (fingernails) or 12–24 weeks (toenails). Tinea pedis: 250 mg daily for 2–6 weeks (oral) or topical cream twice daily for 7–14 days.
1 % cream twice daily for 1–2 weeks; effective for tinea corporis / cruris / pedis.

paediatric.frequency: Children: 62.5–250 mg/day weight-banded (≥ 20 kg).

pregnancy.notes: Avoid where possible (limited data); defer treatment until post-partum.

lactation: Avoid systemic; topical acceptable away from breast.
warnings: Hepatotoxicity — check baseline LFT, repeat at 4–6 weeks; stop if ALT > 3× ULN.
Taste loss (rare but can be prolonged).
Drug interactions — inhibits CYP2D6 (TCAs, beta-blockers, SSRIs).
monitoring: LFT baseline + at 4–6 weeks of oral therapy.

indications.text: Secondary skin infections with Staphylococcus aureus

mechanism: Inhibits bacterial protein synthesis by binding elongation factor G; predominantly active against Gram-positive cocci (especially S. aureus including MSSA).

adult.regimen: Apply thinly to affected area 3–4 times daily for up to 7 days. If no improvement after 7 days, switch to oral antibiotic + reassess.

paediatric.frequency: Same regimen.

pregnancy.notes: Acceptable (minimal absorption).

lactation: Compatible — but avoid application to breast / nipple if breastfeeding.
warnings: Antibiotic stewardship — emerging fusidic-acid-resistant S. aureus; limit course to 7 days. Do NOT use widely / prophylactically.

indications.text: Acute migraine attack (with or without aura)

mechanism: 5-HT1B (cranial vasoconstriction) + 5-HT1D (inhibition of trigeminal nociceptive neurones) agonism.

adult.regimen: 50–100 mg orally as soon as migraine starts; may repeat after 2 h (max 300 mg / 24 h).
Cluster / severe migraine: 6 mg SC; max 12 mg / 24 h.
10–20 mg intranasal; may repeat after 2 h.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data — paracetamol first-line. Where triptan necessary, sumatriptan has the most safety data.

lactation: Express + discard breastmilk for 12 h after SC dose.
contraindications: Concurrent MAOI within 14 days, ergotamine within 24 h, another triptan within 24 h.
warnings: Serotonin syndrome with SSRIs / SNRIs / MAOIs / tramadol / linezolid.
Medication-overuse headache — limit to 8 days/month max.

adverseEffects.effect: Tingling, flushing, chest tightness, fatigue, drowsiness

monitoring: Headache diary; assess CV risk before first prescription.

references.label: NICE CG150 — Headaches in over-12s (2021 update)

indications.text: Bipolar disorder — acute mania + long-term prophylaxis

mechanism: Monovalent cation; inhibits inositol monophosphatase + GSK-3β.

adult.regimen: Start 400 mg modified-release at night (200 mg in elderly / CKD); titrate to serum 0.6–0.8 mmol/L (0.8–1.0 in acute mania).

pregnancy.notes: Ebstein's anomaly risk first trimester (~1 %); specialist decision; alternative lamotrigine / antipsychotic.

lactation: Avoid; if essential monitor infant Li + TSH + creatinine.
warnings: Narrow therapeutic index — toxicity > 1.2 mmol/L. Dehydration / new diuretic / NSAID / ACE-i can precipitate toxicity.
Hypothyroidism, nephrogenic DI, weight gain.
Severe toxicity > 2.0 → dialysis.
monitoring: Serum Li 12 h post-dose at week 1, 4, then 3-monthly; TSH + U&E + Ca + creatinine 6-monthly.

adult.regimen: Start 100–200 mg twice daily; titrate weekly to 800–1200 mg/day in 2–3 doses.

paediatric.frequency: 5 mg/kg/day in 2 doses, titrate to 10–20 mg/kg/day.

pregnancy.notes: Teratogenic (NTDs, ~6 % malformation). Switch to lamotrigine / levetiracetam pre-conception; folic acid 5 mg.

warnings: HLA-B*1502 SJS / TEN risk — screen in Han Chinese / Thai / Malay ancestry.
Potent inducer: reduces OCP, warfarin, atorvastatin, dolutegravir, methadone.
Hyponatraemia (SIADH-like).

adverseEffects.effect: Diplopia, dizziness, drowsiness, ataxia, GI upset

monitoring: FBC + LFT + U&E at 1 month, then 6-monthly.

pregnancy.notes: Limited human data; weak teratogenic signal.

Withdrawal seizures on abrupt stop — taper.
Dependence / misuse.

pregnancy.notes: Acceptable short-term; neonatal withdrawal on chronic use.

lactation: AVOID — infant deaths in CYP2D6 ultra-rapid mothers.
warnings: Constipation prophylaxis.
Variable analgesic effect (CYP2D6 polymorphism).
Dependence.

Cancer pain: 25 µg/h patch every 72 h after stable opioid requirement; always with breakthrough rescue.

Chest-wall rigidity at high IV doses.
Patches in opioid-naïve patients can be fatal.
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors raise exposure substantially.
monitoring: RR, SpO₂, sedation continuous during IV.

10 mg IV slow over 3 min — pre-op or acute migraine.

pregnancy.notes: First / second-trimester hyperemesis acceptable.

warnings: MAX 5 days per EMA / FDA — EPS risk.
QT prolongation — concurrent QT drugs.
Tardive dyskinesia with prolonged use.

Rinse mouth after dose.
High-dose chronic — adrenal suppression, growth-velocity reduction.

Different strengths (100 vs 300 U/mL) — confirm device.
