adult.regimen: Zoster: 1 g three times daily for 7 days (within 72 h of rash). HSV first episode: 500 mg twice daily for 10 days. Recurrent HSV: 500 mg twice daily for 3 days. Suppression: 500 mg once daily.

pregnancy.notes: Safe across pregnancy; first-line for HSV / VZV in pregnancy.

warnings: AKI risk in dehydration / elderly — maintain hydration.
Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura reported in immunocompromised.
monitoring: Creatinine for prolonged courses.

mechanism: Inhibits bacterial isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase → blocks protein synthesis. Active against S. aureus (including MRSA), S. pyogenes.

adult.regimen: Cream apply thinly three times daily for 5 days. Nasal: apply 2 % ointment to each nostril twice daily for 5 days (MRSA decolonisation).

paediatric.frequency: Same regimen.

pregnancy.notes: Safe (minimal absorption).

warnings: Stewardship: emerging resistance with widespread use; limit to 5 days. Reserve for genuine MRSA decolonisation in clinical / outbreak settings.

indications.text: MRSA skin / soft tissue infection (oral / IV)
MDR-TB / XDR-TB (component of BPaL / longer regimen)

mechanism: Binds 50S ribosomal subunit → prevents formation of 70S initiation complex. Bacteriostatic; bactericidal against streptococci.

adult.regimen: 600 mg twice daily (100 % oral bioavailability — same dose IV).
600 mg every 12 h.

paediatric.frequency: 10 mg/kg every 8 h (< 12 y) or every 12 h (≥ 12 y).

pregnancy.notes: Limited human data; reserve for MDR-TB / VRE where no alternative.

contraindications: Concurrent serotonergic agent without close monitoring (SSRIs, SNRIs, TCAs, MAOIs, triptans, tramadol, fentanyl, pethidine, methylene blue, St John's wort).
warnings: Linezolid is a REVERSIBLE MAOI — serotonin syndrome with serotonergics, hypertensive crisis with tyramine-rich foods (aged cheese, beer, soy).
Myelosuppression (thrombocytopenia, anaemia) — risk increases > 14 days. Weekly FBC.
Peripheral + optic neuropathy with > 28-day use.
Lactic acidosis (rare).

adverseEffects.effect: Serotonin syndrome, lactic acidosis, severe myelosuppression

monitoring: FBC weekly. Visual + neurological symptoms reviewed; eye exam if > 28 days.

indications.text: Chloroquine-resistant uncomplicated malaria (oral, with doxycycline / clindamycin)

mechanism: Inhibits parasite haem polymerisation → free haem accumulates → parasite death.

adult.regimen: Loading: 20 mg/kg infused over 4 h (max 1.4 g). Then 10 mg/kg every 8 h over 4 h. Switch to oral when tolerated to complete 7 days.
Oral: 600 mg three times daily for 7 days + doxycycline 200 mg/day or clindamycin 7 days.

paediatric.frequency: Same weight-banded dosing as adults.

pregnancy.notes: Used in severe malaria in pregnancy when IV artesunate unavailable (artesunate preferred per WHO 2023).

warnings: Cinchonism — tinnitus, headache, nausea, blurred vision (dose-related).
QT prolongation + risk of torsades — concurrent QT drugs.
Hypoglycaemia — stimulates pancreatic insulin release; rebound common in pregnancy / severe malaria.
Haemolysis in G6PD-deficient.
monitoring: Continuous ECG during IV infusion. Glucose every 4 h. Daily parasitaemia.

indications.text: Radical cure of P. vivax / P. ovale (eliminates liver hypnozoites)
Single low-dose gametocytocide for P. falciparum transmission blocking (WHO 2012)

mechanism: Active metabolite (carboxyprimaquine) generates reactive oxygen species in plasmodial mitochondria — kills hypnozoites + gametocytes.

adult.regimen: P. vivax / ovale radical cure: 30 mg base once daily for 14 days (G6PD-normal). Falciparum transmission block: 0.25 mg/kg single dose.

paediatric.frequency: 0.5 mg/kg/day for 14 days (G6PD-normal).

pregnancy.notes: Avoid in pregnancy + breastfeeding (foetal G6PD status unknown). Use chloroquine prophylaxis 1×/week throughout pregnancy + radical cure post-partum if G6PD-normal.

warnings: G6PD testing MANDATORY before standard dosing — quantitative (not just qualitative) preferred in females (X-linked heterozygotes can be partial deficiency).
Single low dose (0.25 mg/kg) for P. falciparum transmission blocking is WHO-safe in mild G6PD deficiency.
Methaemoglobinaemia (CYP2D6 poor-metaboliser).
monitoring: G6PD status before dosing. Hb at day 7 of treatment if G6PD-intermediate.

indications.text: Melioidosis (Burkholderia pseudomallei — endemic in SE Asia)

mechanism: PBP-3 binding cell-wall inhibition; potent activity against Pseudomonas but weak Gram-positive cover.

adult.regimen: 1–2 g IV every 8 h (max 6 g/day). Melioidosis intensive phase: 50 mg/kg every 6 h × 2 weeks.

paediatric.frequency: 50 mg/kg every 8 h (max 6 g/day).

pregnancy.notes: Safe for serious infection.

warnings: Less Gram-positive cover than ceftriaxone — not for streptococcal / staphylococcal monotherapy.
Neurotoxicity (encephalopathy) in renal impairment.
monitoring: FBC, U&E, LFT.

mechanism: 30S ribosomal binding — same as gentamicin; broader Gram-negative cover including some gentamicin-resistant strains.

adult.regimen: 15 mg/kg ideal body weight once daily; target peak 25–35 mg/L, trough < 5 mg/L.

paediatric.frequency: 15 mg/kg once daily.

renal.adjustment: Same dose, extend interval to 36 h with TDM.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data — same fetal cranial nerve VIII risk as gentamicin.

warnings: Nephro + ototoxic — same precautions as gentamicin (TDM, avoid concurrent loop diuretic / vancomycin).
monitoring: Trough pre-dose; eGFR daily; audiology if > 7 days.

mechanism: B28 Pro → Asp substitution → does not self-associate as hexamer → rapid SC absorption (onset 10–20 min, peak 1–3 h, duration 3–5 h).

adult.regimen: Pre-meal: 0.05–0.15 U/kg per meal titrated to post-prandial glucose < 10 mmol/L. Inject 5–10 min before meal (or with the meal). Total daily insulin 0.5–1 U/kg in T1DM (50 % basal / 50 % bolus split).

paediatric.frequency: Same per-kg dose as adults; carbohydrate-counting ratios from ~ 1 U per 12 g in adolescents.

pregnancy.notes: Safer than regular insulin in pregnancy (less post-prandial hypoglycaemia).

warnings: Take immediately before meal — earlier than regular insulin.
Lipohypertrophy if injection sites not rotated.
monitoring: Capillary glucose 4–6× daily on multi-dose injection regimen.

indications.text: Newborn vitamin K deficiency bleeding prevention
Vitamin K deficiency in cholestatic liver disease / malabsorption

mechanism: Cofactor for hepatic γ-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X + proteins C and S.

adult.regimen: Warfarin reversal: 1–10 mg IV slow (over ≥ 30 sec). Major bleed: 10 mg IV + PCC 25–50 IU/kg. Asymptomatic INR 5–8: 1–2.5 mg oral. INR > 8: 1–5 mg oral.
Cholestatic liver disease: 10 mg orally weekly.

paediatric.frequency: Newborn prophylaxis: 1 mg IM single dose within 1 h of birth (UK + WHO). Oral alternative 2 mg at birth, day 4–7, and 1 month (less effective; reserved for parental refusal of IM).

pregnancy.notes: Safe; given to mother on warfarin / phenytoin in last 4 weeks to prevent neonatal haemorrhage.

contraindications: Hypersensitivity (anaphylactoid reaction to IV preparation rare).
warnings: Slow IV administration (anaphylactoid reactions reported with rapid push).
IV / IM preferred over subcutaneous (unreliable absorption).
Recheck INR at 6–12 h after vitamin K administration in warfarin reversal.
monitoring: INR 6–12 h after dose in warfarin reversal.

indications.text: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) — prevention + treatment

mechanism: Replaces deficient endogenous surfactant → reduces alveolar surface tension → prevents end-expiratory collapse, improves compliance + oxygenation.

paediatric.frequency: RDS treatment: 200 mg/kg (2.5 mL/kg) endotracheal initial dose. Second / third doses 100 mg/kg every 6–12 h if continuing oxygen requirement. Total max 3 doses. Less-invasive surfactant administration (LISA) preferred over INSURE technique.

pregnancy.notes: Not applicable (neonatal use).

contraindications: Pulmonary haemorrhage at time of administration (relative).
warnings: Transient airway obstruction during dosing — reflux up the tube; pause and resume.
Transient bradycardia / desaturation during administration.
Risk of pulmonary haemorrhage — particularly in PDA-shunting infants.
monitoring: Continuous SpO₂, ECG, respiratory rate during + after administration.

references.label: European Consensus Guidelines on Management of RDS (2023)

indications.text: Emergency contraception within 72 h of unprotected intercourse

mechanism: Primarily inhibits / delays ovulation. Less effective post-ovulation. Does NOT terminate established pregnancy.

adult.regimen: 1.5 mg single dose within 72 h of unprotected intercourse (sooner = more effective; 95 % efficacy < 24 h). Repeat dose if vomits within 3 h.

pregnancy.notes: Not abortifacient. Safe if accidentally taken after conception — no teratogenic signal.

warnings: Reduced efficacy if BMI > 26 (or weight > 70 kg) — consider doubling to 3 mg OR using ulipristal acetate (30 mg) OR copper IUD (most effective).
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, ritonavir, St John's wort) reduce efficacy — use copper IUD as alternative.
If menses delayed > 7 days → urine pregnancy test.
monitoring: Pregnancy test if menses delayed > 7 days.

indications.text: Medical termination of pregnancy (with misoprostol) up to 70 days gestation
Medical management of missed / incomplete miscarriage
Cervical priming before surgical termination / induction of labour

mechanism: Competitive progesterone-receptor antagonist → decidual breakdown + cervical softening + increased uterine sensitivity to prostaglandins.

adult.regimen: MTOP ≤ 70 days: 200 mg orally, followed 24–48 h later by misoprostol 800 µg buccal / vaginal / sublingual. Missed miscarriage: 200 mg orally + misoprostol 800 µg 24–48 h later.

pregnancy.notes: Used DURING pregnancy for intentional termination only. AVOID if continuing pregnancy.

lactation: Brief interruption of breastfeeding (4 h) acceptable.
warnings: Rare severe bacterial sepsis (Clostridium sordellii) — counsel return for severe pain, weakness, prolonged bleeding.
Significant bleeding (10–20 % require additional intervention, 1–2 % surgical evacuation, 0.3 % transfusion).
Confirm completion at 7–14 days (urine pregnancy test or follow-up).

adverseEffects.effect: Vaginal bleeding (heavier than menses 5–14 days), abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea

monitoring: Confirm completion at 7–14 days. Beta-hCG decline / repeat scan if uncertain. Counsel about future contraception.

mechanism: Suppresses ovulation + thickens cervical mucus + thins endometrium.

adult.regimen: 150 mg IM every 12 weeks (Depo-Provera) OR 104 mg subcutaneous every 13 weeks (Sayana Press — self-administered).

pregnancy.notes: Not for use during pregnancy.

lactation: Compatible. Can be initiated immediately post-partum, including in breastfeeding women.
warnings: Bone-mineral-density loss (partly reversible) — consider use < 2 years where alternative available; not first-line in adolescents / women > 45.
Weight gain common (~ 2 kg / 1st year).
Return to fertility delayed up to 12 months after stopping (mean 5 months).
Counsel breakthrough bleeding.

adverseEffects.effect: Amenorrhoea, irregular bleeding, weight gain, mood disturbance
Reduced BMD, delayed return of fertility

monitoring: BP at each visit; review every 2 years for ongoing need (BMD).

mechanism: Oestrogen + progestogen → suppress hypothalamic GnRH → suppress LH surge → no ovulation.

adult.regimen: Take 1 tablet daily at same time for 21 days, then 7-day break (or continuous extended-cycle 84 + 7). Levonorgestrel 150 µg / ethinylestradiol 30 µg is first-line low-strength preparation.

pregnancy.notes: Not for use during pregnancy.

lactation: AVOID until ≥ 6 weeks post-partum + good lactation established (reduces milk supply). Progestogen-only preferred.
contraindications: History of VTE / arterial thrombosis / known thrombophilia.
warnings: VTE risk 3–5× background (highest in first year and after restart).
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, ritonavir, St John's wort) reduce contraceptive efficacy → use alternative.
Missed pill rules — emergency contraception if > 1 pill missed in week 1.

adverseEffects.effect: Nausea, breast tenderness, breakthrough bleeding, mood change, headache

monitoring: BP at start + 3 months + annually.

references.label: WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use

indications.text: Iron-deficiency anaemia — intolerance / malabsorption / urgent / severe (Hb < 8 + symptomatic)
Heart failure with iron deficiency (CONFIRM-HF trial)

mechanism: Slow release of iron from carboxymaltose complex → bypasses GI absorption → restores iron stores within hours.

adult.regimen: Up to 1000 mg in a single infusion (maximum 20 mg/kg) given over ≥ 15 min. Repeat 1 week later if total replacement needs > 1000 mg.

pregnancy.notes: Safe from second trimester onwards. Particularly useful in third trimester for rapid correction before delivery.

warnings: Hypersensitivity / anaphylaxis (rare but reported) — observe 30 min post-infusion. Resuscitation equipment + adrenaline available.
Hypophosphataemia (often asymptomatic, may persist months) — check phosphate at 2 weeks + 3 months if repeated infusions.
Skin discoloration if extravasation.
monitoring: Hb + ferritin at 6–8 weeks. Phosphate at 2 weeks + 3 months if repeat doses.

references.label: ESC Heart Failure Guidelines (iron in HFrEF)

mechanism: Inhibits bacterial dihydropteroate synthase + has anti-neutrophil / anti-inflammatory effects in dermatologic indications.

adult.regimen: PJP prophylaxis: 100 mg once daily. Leprosy MB: 100 mg daily. Dermatitis herpetiformis: start 50 mg daily, titrate to effect (max 300 mg).

paediatric.frequency: 1 mg/kg/day (PJP / leprosy).

pregnancy.notes: Acceptable for leprosy / dermatitis herpetiformis; add folic acid 5 mg.

lactation: Acceptable; observe infant for haemolysis if G6PD-deficient.
warnings: G6PD screening before starting — methaemoglobinaemia + haemolysis.
Dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome (fever, rash, lymphadenopathy, hepatitis) — HLA-B*1301 risk in Asian populations.
Methaemoglobinaemia + sulfhaemoglobinaemia common — monitor SpO₂ vs PaO₂ gap.
Peripheral neuropathy with chronic use.

adverseEffects.effect: Dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome, severe haemolysis (G6PD), agranulocytosis

monitoring: FBC + reticulocytes + methaemoglobin at 1 month then 6-monthly. LFT 3-monthly.

indications.text: Asthma maintenance — always in combination with ICS (never monotherapy)

mechanism: Selective β2-receptor agonist → bronchodilation (onset 10–20 min, duration 12 h).

adult.regimen: 50 µg twice daily (max 100 µg twice daily). Always in combination with ICS for asthma — never monotherapy (SMART trial — increased asthma deaths).

paediatric.frequency: Age ≥ 5: 50 µg twice daily, always with ICS.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data; ICS + LABA continued for asthma control.

contraindications: Asthma without concurrent ICS (FDA / EMA boxed warning).
warnings: ASTHMA: NEVER as monotherapy — increases mortality. Always combination ICS+LABA inhaler.
β-blocker (propranolol — non-selective) antagonises bronchodilation.
QT prolongation at high doses, tremor, palpitations.
monitoring: Symptom control, inhaler technique, FEV1.

indications.text: COPD maintenance — reduces exacerbations + improves FEV1
Severe asthma (add-on to ICS + LABA, ≥ 6 years)

mechanism: Selective M3 muscarinic-receptor antagonist → bronchodilation. Long duration (24 h).

adult.regimen: 18 µg via HandiHaler OR 5 µg via Respimat once daily, same time each day.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data; only if benefit > risk.

warnings: Acute angle-closure glaucoma — counsel ocular pain, halos.
Urinary retention in BPH.
AVOID concurrent inhaled ipratropium (additive anticholinergic).
monitoring: FEV1, exacerbation frequency, intra-ocular symptoms.

indications.text: Paediatric / neonatal hypoglycaemia (preferred over 50 % in children — avoids sclerosis)

mechanism: Cellular substrate — restores plasma glucose; less sclerotic than 50 % in small veins.

adult.regimen: Adult hypoglycaemia: 100 mL of 10 % IV bolus over 5 min (10 g glucose); alternative to 50 % when small vein. Sulphonylurea maintenance: 5–10 % infusion at maintenance + 50 % above with octreotide.

paediatric.frequency: Hypoglycaemia: 2 mL/kg of 10 % IV bolus, recheck at 5 + 15 min. Neonatal maintenance: 60–80 mL/kg/day of 10 % dextrose in the first 24 h.

pregnancy.notes: Safe.

warnings: Rebound hypoglycaemia after bolus alone — follow with 10 % infusion + recheck.
Hyperglycaemic stress in critical illness — target glucose 7–10 mmol/L.
monitoring: Glucose every 15 min post-bolus + hourly during infusion.

indications.text: Opioid use disorder — opioid agonist therapy (OAT)

mechanism: Full µ-opioid agonist; long half-life (24–55 h). Cross-tolerant with heroin / morphine — blocks withdrawal + reduces craving + occupies receptors so additional opioid has no effect.

adult.regimen: OAT initiation: 10–30 mg orally on day 1 (titrate based on objective opioid withdrawal scale + tolerance). Titrate by 5–10 mg every 3–5 days to effective dose (typically 60–120 mg/day). Daily-supervised dispensing first 3 months.

pregnancy.notes: Maintain or initiate methadone in pregnancy (avoiding withdrawal prevents miscarriage / preterm labour). Dose may need increase in third trimester (split BID). Neonatal abstinence syndrome managed in neonatal unit.

warnings: QT prolongation — torsades de pointes risk especially > 100 mg/day; baseline + 30 days + annual ECG. Avoid with QT drugs (azithromycin, fluconazole, ondansetron, haloperidol, amiodarone, clarithromycin).
Respiratory depression — high risk in early induction (long half-life accumulates over 5–7 days).
Severe drug interactions — CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin) → withdrawal; inhibitors → toxicity.
Overdose — naloxone repeated / infusion due to long methadone half-life.

adverseEffects.effect: Torsades de pointes, respiratory depression, overdose death

monitoring: ECG at baseline, 30 days, annually + dose > 100 mg. Urine drug screen periodic. Pregnancy test where applicable.

references.label: NICE TA114 — Methadone + buprenorphine for opioid dependence

indications.text: Opioid use disorder — OAT (alternative to methadone, often preferred for safety)

mechanism: High-affinity partial µ-agonist with ceiling effect on respiratory depression (safer than full agonist in overdose). Displaces other opioids — can precipitate withdrawal if started too soon after heroin / methadone.

adult.regimen: Induction (must be in mild objective withdrawal, COWS ≥ 7): 4 mg sublingually, second 4 mg dose 2–4 h later (total 8 mg day 1). Titrate to 8–16 mg/day; max 32 mg. Suboxone (with naloxone) preferred to deter injection misuse.

pregnancy.notes: Buprenorphine acceptable; less neonatal abstinence severity than methadone (MOTHER trial). Use mono-buprenorphine (Subutex) — Suboxone naloxone has limited safety data.

warnings: Precipitated withdrawal — start ONLY when in objective opioid withdrawal (12–24 h after last short-acting opioid; 36–48 h after methadone).
Hepatic injury — LFTs at baseline + periodic.
Sublingual administration — DO NOT swallow; takes 5–10 min to dissolve.
monitoring: LFT baseline + 6-monthly. Urine drug screen periodic.

indications.text: Opioid use disorder — relapse prevention (after detoxification)
Alcohol use disorder — reduces heavy-drinking days, craving

mechanism: Pure opioid antagonist — blocks reinforcing effects of opioids. In alcohol disorder, blocks endogenous opioid reward.

adult.regimen: Alcohol / opioid: 50 mg orally once daily. Start AFTER at least 7 days opioid-free (10 days methadone) — naloxone challenge to confirm.
Vivitrol depot: 380 mg IM monthly.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data; only if benefit > risk.

contraindications: Current opioid use / dependence (precipitates severe withdrawal).
warnings: Precipitates SEVERE withdrawal if started < 7 days opioid-free.
Patients who relapse have lost tolerance — increased overdose death risk.
Counsel: in emergency needing opioid analgesia, use 2–3× normal dose carefully or non-opioid alternative.
Hepatotoxicity at high doses.

adverseEffects.effect: Severe opioid withdrawal (in dependent users), hepatotoxicity (high dose)

monitoring: LFT baseline + 3-monthly.

references.label: NICE TA115 — Naltrexone for opioid dependence

indications.text: Severe pain (acute trauma, war / disaster setting)

mechanism: NMDA receptor antagonism + opioid-mu agonism + monoamine reuptake inhibition. Preserves airway reflexes + spontaneous breathing.

adult.regimen: Procedural sedation: 1–2 mg/kg IV over 1 min, supplement 0.5 mg/kg as needed. Analgesia (sub-dissociative): 0.1–0.3 mg/kg IV / IM. Induction for intubation: 1–2 mg/kg IV.
Procedural sedation: 4–5 mg/kg IM.

paediatric.frequency: Sedation: 1 mg/kg IV (or 4–5 mg/kg IM).

pregnancy.notes: Reserve for serious indication; theoretical neurodevelopmental concerns from prolonged exposure.

contraindications: Raised intracranial pressure (debated — recent evidence weak).
warnings: Emergence phenomena (hallucinations, vivid dreams) — pre-medicate with low-dose midazolam in adults if elective sedation.
Hypersalivation — atropine / glycopyrrolate pre-medication.
Counsel risk of street ketamine misuse (urinary tract toxicity).

adverseEffects.effect: Emergence phenomena, hypersalivation, nystagmus, hypertension, tachycardia

monitoring: Continuous SpO₂, ECG, BP during dissociative sedation.

mechanism: GABA-A receptor positive modulator → CNS depression. Rapid onset (30 sec), brief duration.

adult.regimen: Induction: 1.5–2.5 mg/kg slow IV (lower in elderly / shock). ICU sedation: 0.3–4 mg/kg/h titrated. AVOID > 4 mg/kg/h for > 48 h (PRIS risk).

paediatric.frequency: Induction 2.5–3.5 mg/kg ≥ 3 y. ICU sedation > 16 y only.

pregnancy.notes: Used in obstetric anaesthesia; neonatal depression if delivered close to induction.

contraindications: ICU sedation in paediatric patients < 16 y (PRIS).
warnings: Hypotension on induction — fluid bolus + reduce dose in shock.
Apnoea — be ready to ventilate.
Propofol-related infusion syndrome (PRIS) — high-dose long-duration; metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, AKI, hyperkalaemia. Limit dose > 4 mg/kg/h to < 48 h.
Counsel: green discolouration of urine harmless.
monitoring: Continuous BP, SpO₂, ECG. CK + lactate + ABG if prolonged high-dose infusion.

indications.text: Fever where oral route not available

mechanism: Same as oral — central COX inhibition.

adult.regimen: 1 g IV infusion over 15 min every 6 h (max 4 g/24 h). Reduce to 500 mg if < 50 kg.

paediatric.frequency: 15 mg/kg every 6 h (max 4 doses/24 h).

pregnancy.notes: Safe — same as oral.

warnings: Dose errors more common with IV (mg vs mL confusion) — double-check.
Underweight adults < 50 kg → max 60 mg/kg/day.
Hepatotoxicity same as oral in overdose.
monitoring: LFT for prolonged courses, or in malnutrition / alcohol / hepatic disease.

indications.text: COPD with frequent exacerbations / eosinophilic phenotype

mechanism: Local glucocorticoid receptor activation → anti-inflammatory airway effect. Strong topical potency, low oral bioavailability (high first-pass), reduced systemic effects.

adult.regimen: Asthma: low dose 200–400 µg/day; medium 400–800 µg/day; high 800–1600 µg/day in 1–2 divided doses.
Croup: 2 mg nebulised single dose (children). Acute asthma adjunct in some protocols.

paediatric.frequency: Children 5–11 y low 100–200 µg/day, medium 200–400, high > 400 — always via spacer.

pregnancy.notes: Safe — preferred ICS in pregnancy; most safety data of any ICS.

warnings: Inhaler-technique check every visit; use spacer for pMDI.
Rinse mouth after each dose (oral candidiasis, dysphonia).
High-dose long-term: HPA-axis suppression, growth velocity reduction in children, cataracts.
monitoring: Asthma control, growth velocity in children, inhaler technique.

indications.text: Ulcerative colitis — induction + maintenance of remission
Crohn's colitis (less effective than for UC)

mechanism: Inhibits NF-κB + lipoxygenase + cyclo-oxygenase pathways in colonic mucosa; topical effect.

adult.regimen: UC induction: 2.4–4.8 g/day in divided doses. Maintenance: 1.5–2.4 g/day. Modified-release formulations target ileum / colon.
Distal UC: enema 1 g at bedtime OR suppository 500 mg three times daily for 4–6 weeks.

pregnancy.notes: Safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding — first-line UC maintenance.

warnings: Renal toxicity (interstitial nephritis) — check eGFR baseline + annually.
Blood dyscrasias (rare) — counsel sore throat, fever, bleeding.
Pancreatitis (rare).

adverseEffects.effect: Nausea, headache, abdominal pain, diarrhoea (paradoxically can worsen colitis)
Interstitial nephritis, hepatitis, pancreatitis, blood dyscrasias

monitoring: FBC + U&E + LFT baseline, at 3 months, then annually.

mechanism: Same as simvastatin — minimal CYP3A4 (mainly CYP2C9 + OATP1B1) → fewer DDIs.

adult.regimen: 5–40 mg once daily. Start 10 mg, titrate by LDL response. Reduce in Asian descent (genetic OATP1B1 — higher exposure).

pregnancy.notes: Avoid in pregnancy + breastfeeding.

warnings: Less affected by CYP3A4 inhibitors than simvastatin / atorvastatin.
Proteinuria + microscopic haematuria at high doses (40 mg).
Asian populations — higher AUC; start lower.
monitoring: LFT baseline + 3 + 12 months.

mechanism: Direct competitive inhibitor of free + clot-bound thrombin (factor IIa).

adult.regimen: AF: 150 mg twice daily (110 mg if age ≥ 80, increased bleed risk, or concurrent verapamil). DVT/PE: 5–10 days of parenteral anticoagulation then 150 mg twice daily.

pregnancy.notes: Avoid; use LMWH in pregnancy.

warnings: P-gp inhibitors (verapamil, amiodarone, clarithromycin, dronedarone, ketoconazole) raise levels.
Reversal: idarucizumab (Praxbind) 5 g IV — specific antidote.
Dyspepsia common — take with full glass of water.
monitoring: eGFR + Hb 6-monthly.

mechanism: Selective direct factor Xa inhibition.

adult.regimen: 60 mg once daily. Reduce to 30 mg if any of: CrCl 15–50, weight ≤ 60 kg, concurrent strong P-gp inhibitor (verapamil, dronedarone, clarithromycin, ketoconazole).

pregnancy.notes: Avoid; use LMWH.

contraindications: eGFR > 95 in AF (reduced efficacy vs warfarin).
warnings: P-gp inhibitor / inducer interaction.
DVT/PE needs 5–10 days parenteral first.
monitoring: eGFR + Hb 6-monthly.

mechanism: Inhibits Na-Cl co-transporter in distal tubule + vasodilation.

adult.regimen: 1.5 mg modified-release once daily (or 2.5 mg standard).

pregnancy.notes: Avoid first-line (volume depletion, electrolyte shift).

warnings: Hyponatraemia in elderly — check Na at 1 + 4 weeks of initiation.
Hyperuricaemia + gout flare.
QT prolongation at high doses.
monitoring: U&E + Na at 1 + 4 weeks then 6-monthly.

indications.text: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage — prevention of cerebral vasospasm + ischaemic neurological deficit

mechanism: L-type Ca channel blockade with preferential cerebrovascular effect.

adult.regimen: 60 mg every 4 h orally for 21 days starting within 96 h of SAH. NG if unable to swallow.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data; SAH is critical — use.

warnings: Hypotension common — adjust other antihypertensives.
Do NOT give IV (cardiac arrest reports).
monitoring: BP every 4 h during therapy.

indications.text: Raised intracranial pressure (TBI, stroke, hepatic encephalopathy)

mechanism: Inert osmotic agent — pulls fluid from intracellular / interstitial space → cerebral oedema reduction.

adult.regimen: Raised ICP: 0.5–1 g/kg of 20 % over 15 min, repeat every 4–6 h targeting osmolality 300–320 mOsm/L. Glaucoma: 1–2 g/kg over 30 min.

paediatric.frequency: 0.5–1 g/kg over 15 min, repeat every 4–6 h.

pregnancy.notes: Use only if benefit > risk; limited data.

warnings: Rebound ICP rise after stopping — taper.
Hyperosmolality, hypovolaemia, hypernatraemia + AKI risk.
Check osmolality + electrolytes every 6 h.
monitoring: Serum osmolality 6-hourly (target 300–320); Na, K, creatinine; urine output.

mechanism: Long-acting somatostatin analogue — inhibits GH, glucagon, insulin, splanchnic blood flow.

adult.regimen: Variceal bleed: 50 µg IV bolus + 50 µg/h infusion × 3–5 days.
Sulphonylurea overdose: 50–100 µg SC every 6 h × 24 h. Carcinoid: 50–250 µg SC three times daily.

pregnancy.notes: Limited data; reserve for serious indication.

warnings: Hyperglycaemia (suppresses insulin) — monitor glucose.
Gallstones (long-term use).
Bradycardia.
monitoring: Glucose during infusion. Thyroid + gallbladder USS for long-term.

indications.text: Acute oesophageal variceal bleeding (preferred over octreotide where available)

mechanism: V1-receptor agonist → splanchnic vasoconstriction → ↓ portal pressure.
